classification.difficultyReason: Form a journey-cost model from hourly cost and travel time, differentiate a reciprocal expression, verify the minimum and interpret the result.

content.prompt: A transport company runs a truck from Hobart to Launceston, a distance of 250 km, at a constant speed of $v$ km/h. For a given speed $v$, the cost per hour is $6400+v^2$ cents.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the cost of the trip, in cents, is $C=250\left(\frac{6400}{v}+v\right)$.

answer.worked:
The time for the trip is
$$\begin{align*}\text{time}&=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}\\\text{time}&=\frac{250}{v}\text{ hours}.\end{align*}$$
Hence
$$\begin{align*}C&=(\text{cost per hour})\times(\text{time for trip})\\C&=(6400+v^2)\times\frac{250}{v}\\C&=250\left(\frac{6400}{v}+v\right).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the speed at which the cost of the journey is minimised.

answer.worked:
For $v>0$,
$$\begin{align*}C&=250\left(\frac{6400}{v}+v\right)\\\frac{dC}{dv}&=250\left(-\frac{6400}{v^2}+1\right)\\\frac{dC}{dv}&=\frac{250(v^2-6400)}{v^2}\\\frac{dC}{dv}&=\frac{250(v-80)(v+80)}{v^2}.\end{align*}$$
The derivative has a single zero in the domain $v>0$, at $v=80$.
$$\frac{d^2C}{dv^2}=\frac{250\times12800}{v^3}>0\qquad(v>0).$$
Therefore $v=80$ gives the global minimum in this domain. The speed is $80\text{ km/h}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the minimum cost of the journey.
